Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Machine Learning

tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with six years of experience in analytics and data science, including more than four years as a data scientist. Builds forecasting and customer models in Python and SQL, with experience in feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring and automated testing. Strong statistical background and a track record of translating analysis into operational decisions. Moving towards machine learning engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python: pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, pytest, Streamlit; PyTorch and torchvision (course project)
Data and cloud tools: SQL, BigQuery, dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker
Engineering tools: Git, Docker (Dockerfile for Streamlit app), Jupyter
Methods: feature engineering, model evaluation, time-series forecasting, A/B testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics
R: tidyverse, brms, R Markdown

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox, Edinburgh | Feb 2022–Present
- Built a LightGBM demand forecasting model for weekly orders by recipe and region, six weeks ahead. Engineered calendar, price and menu-position features; reduced WAPE from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%.
- Ran forecasting as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writing to BigQuery, with results available to operations in Looker.
- Started writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025, reaching approximately 60% coverage.
- Built an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers. A 10% holdout showed churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Wrote production SQL in BigQuery and maintained dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Designed and analysed approximately 40 A/B tests per year for product and growth teams. Built a Streamlit sequential testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues; wrote its Dockerfile, while the data platform team handled deployment.
- Presented results to leadership monthly and delivered internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail, Glasgow | Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Conducted customer segmentation and tariff analysis in R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports using R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days per month.

PROJECT

Image Classification Course Project | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small convolutional neural network in PyTorch on a public food images dataset, achieving approximately 80% accuracy. Completed as a learning project using torchvision and Google Colab.

EDUCATION

MSc Statistics, Distinction | University of the Lothians | 2020
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019

LANGUAGES
English (native); Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured and professional CV with strong quantified achievements. The forecasting, churn, experimentation and testing examples are specific and credible, and the document appropriately distinguishes the candidate's current data scientist background from a move toward machine learning engineering. The main content limitation is not writing quality but the substantial distance between the candidate's experience and this role's seniority and production-engineering requirements. The summary could present the candidate's operational ML experience more precisely and avoid the vague phrase "customer models."
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly conventional headings, plain text structure, standard date formatting, searchable technology names and no apparent parsing hazards such as tables, graphics or columns. It includes useful terms including Python, SQL, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring, automated testing, Docker, dbt, model evaluation and forecasting. AI screening probability is moderate to low for this particular vacancy because several high-weight terms are absent or unsupported: AI products, chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLOps, and four years of machine learning engineering experience. The cloud evidence is present but should be made more explicit by naming GCP and Cloud Run where accurate.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python, feature engineering, statistical modelling, experimentation, batch ML workflows, GCP-based tools, automated testing and business-focused operational decisions. It also demonstrates relevant ownership, communication and learning through internal training and independent PyTorch study, although culture alignment should not be overstated. The candidate has a relevant quantitative degree, but the stated degree requirement specifically prioritises machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field; Statistics and Mathematics are not a clear match. The candidate's material does not show four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production, AI products such as chat assistants or RAG, production model serving/monitoring/data versioning, or MLOps platforms. The CV does show production-oriented scheduled batch workflows and analytics engineering, but these are not equivalent to the role's full production ML engineering requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The added details are supported by the Original Candidate Information and portfolio; no clear hallucinated skill, tool or experience is present.

MEANINGFUL CV IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace "Builds forecasting and customer models in Python and SQL, with experience in feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring and automated testing" with "Builds and operationalises forecasting and churn propensity models in Python and SQL, including feature engineering, scheduled batch scoring and automated testing." This uses the more precise model names and better reflects the evidence without claiming API deployment or full MLOps ownership.
2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Data and cloud tools: SQL, BigQuery, dbt, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker" to "Cloud and data: GCP (BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run), SQL, dbt, Looker." The candidate's portfolio supports Cloud Run, and naming GCP improves ATS matching while remaining accurate. Do not describe the candidate as having broad GCP infrastructure expertise.
3. In the Technical Skills section, add a separate line after the engineering tools line: "Testing and deployment: pytest, Docker, Streamlit, scheduled notebook workflows, dbt Cloud scheduler." The candidate's notes support pytest, Docker, scheduled notebooks and dbt Cloud scheduling. Do not label these tools as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or MLOps platforms.
4. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the scheduled-workflow bullet to: "Operationalised the LightGBM forecasting workflow as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook writing results to BigQuery, with outputs consumed by operations in Looker." This makes the production-oriented workflow clearer while accurately avoiding a claim of API model serving.
5. In the Thistlebox experience section, add a bullet after the Streamlit bullet: "Wrote the Dockerfile for a Streamlit sequential-testing application used by approximately 25 colleagues; the data platform team deployed it on Cloud Run." This is supported by the portfolio and demonstrates practical software packaging and cloud deployment collaboration without overstating ownership.
6. In the Thistlebox experience section, revise "Wrote production SQL in BigQuery and maintained dbt models for the analytics layer" to "Wrote production SQL in BigQuery and maintained dbt models and scheduled data workflows for the analytics layer." This more directly surfaces the candidate's data-pipeline and orchestration experience, but should not be changed to "data ingestion pipeline" unless the candidate can substantiate ingestion specifically.
7. In the Technical Skills section, retain "PyTorch and torchvision (course project)" but change it to "PyTorch, torchvision (course project; CNN fine-tuning)". This improves keyword specificity while preserving the important limitation that the experience is academic rather than production experience.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, professional and substantially stronger than the original information. It presents quantified outcomes, relevant technologies and credible boundaries around deployment responsibility. The summary is well targeted toward a data scientist-to-machine-learning-engineering transition, and the experience section demonstrates forecasting, churn modelling, feature engineering, experimentation and cloud-based batch workflows. The main content defect is the duplicated Docker/Streamlit achievement. The document also has limited evidence of software engineering beyond testing, Dockerfile creation and scheduled batch workflows, which is important for this particular role but is a candidate-profile gap rather than a writing defect.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text formatting, searchable technology names and a logical reverse-chronological structure. It includes strong matching terms such as Python, SQL, GCP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run, feature engineering, automated testing, Docker, dbt and scheduled workflows. AI screening probability for this specific role is moderate to low because the CV does not contain supported evidence for chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation, language models, model serving, monitoring, data versioning or named MLOps tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow or Airflow. These are genuine experience gaps, not keywords that should be added without evidence. The duplicate Streamlit/Docker bullet may cause redundant parsing and should be removed.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with Python-based machine learning, feature engineering, forecasting, customer analytics, GCP, batch scoring, data workflows and statistical model evaluation. The candidate has more than four years as a data scientist, but the material does not establish four years as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production. The forecasting system is a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook and the churn model is batch-scored in BigQuery; there is no candidate-owned API model serving, monitoring or data versioning evidence. There is also no experience with AI products such as chat assistants or RAG, and no evidence of preparing large text datasets or fine-tuning language models. The MSc Statistics and BSc Mathematics are relevant quantitative degrees, but they are not degrees specifically in machine learning, computer science or engineering. GCP experience is shown, as are Python, feature engineering and analytics data workflows. The CV gives some evidence of orchestration through scheduled notebooks and dbt Cloud scheduling, but not broader MLOps practice. Evidence for the company's ownership, teamwork and learning culture is limited but not required to be invented.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the Professional Experience section under “Data Scientist | Thistlebox,” delete one of the two duplicate bullets beginning “Built a Streamlit sequential testing calculator...” and “Wrote the Dockerfile for a Streamlit sequential-testing application...”. Keep a single combined bullet: “Built a Streamlit sequential-testing calculator used by approximately 25 colleagues; wrote its Dockerfile, while the data platform team deployed it on Cloud Run.” This removes repetition while preserving the truthful deployment boundary.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE: In the Professional Experience section under Thistlebox, make the data-pipeline evidence more explicit without overstating it. Change “Wrote production SQL in BigQuery and maintained dbt models and scheduled data workflows for the analytics layer” to “Wrote production SQL in BigQuery and maintained dbt models and scheduled dbt Cloud workflows supporting analytics data pipelines.”

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE: In the Technical Skills section, add the supported modelling tool “SHAP” to the Python or model-evaluation line, because the candidate portfolio states that SHAP was used for the churn project. For example, change “Python: pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels...” to “Python: pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, statsmodels...”

MINOR: In the Technical Skills section, avoid implying that the candidate has broad production deployment experience. Rename “Testing and deployment” to “Testing and workflow delivery” because the CV itself states that the platform team handled Cloud Run deployment and the candidate's production ML workflows are scheduled batch jobs.
